newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wellington council says Wilson can't buy carparks.
newsitem.headline: Wellington council says Wilson can't buy carparks.

text.p: Shortly after New Zealand's anti-monopolies Commerce Commission gave final clearance to Wilson Parking to buy four central Wellington carparks on Wednesday, the Wellington City Council decided not to sell them.
In a special meeting the council voted ten to seven against selling the four car parking business on the grounds that --
* tenders received did not reflect their long-term income generation potential, and
* their disposal could undermine the council's transport policy with a possible shift from short-stay shopper parking to long-stay commuter parking.

In March, the Commerce Commission had refused Wilson Parking permission to buy the carparks over concerns that it might give Wilson dominance of long-stay casual parking in the capital's business and commercial area.

Following a revised application by the company, commission chairman Allan Bollard said earlier on Wednesday he was satisfied that, subject to divestment of certain other assets by the company, Wilson would not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in any market.
Wilson was not initially avaliable for comment.
